summary: Kickoff for onboarding Peregrine Medical Systems. Customer is highly regulated (PHI), leaning toward Redwood Private in their AWS account but wants to validate latency and rollout plan. Agreed to tech deep-dive and to exchange security artifacts; next step is a performance bench session and pricing follow-up.
transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-12-20 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~50 minutes
Location: Zoom
Meeting link: zoom.us/j/placeholder
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood CSM), Ravi (Redwood Eng), Sofia (Peregrine Head of Data), Ethan (Peregrine Platform Eng), Anika (Clinical Ops), Liam (Security)

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Um, really excited to kick this off with Peregrine. Quick round robin — if you can say name and role.
[00:12] Sofia (Peregrine): Hi, I'm Sofia Morales, Head of Data. We're leading this from the data side.
[00:17] Ethan (Peregrine): Ethan Cole, platform engineering. I'll own infra and the integration work.
[00:22] Anika (Peregrine): Dr. Anika Rao, Clinical Ops — I'll be the clinical sponsor and help validate model outputs.
[00:27] Liam (Peregrine): Liam Brooks, security and compliance. I'll review any security artifacts and run the checklist.
[00:31] Jordan (Redwood): Great. Maya and Ravi?
[00:33] Maya (Redwood): Maya Chen, Customer Success — I'll be your day-to-day contact.
[00:36] Ravi (Redwood): Ravi Patel, implementation engineer, will run the tech deep-dive and the pilot setup.

[02:05] Jordan: Objective for today's call: align on scope, success criteria, timeline, and immediate asks. We know Peregrine handles PHI and has strict data residency needs, so talk through which Redwood deployment you think you want. Sofia, do you want to start with current stack and pain points?
[02:20] Sofia: Sure. Right now we have a mix — some inference on-prem for older models, most new inference is on AWS EKS with custom autoscaling and a homegrown batching layer. Latency is kinda variable, costs are creeping up, and we don't have good visibility into per-route cost. Also audits are basically manual which is a problem for compliance.
[02:42] Jordan: Got it, and what's your orchestration — is it EKS Fargate or managed nodes?
[02:48] Ethan: Managed node groups on EKS, mixed instance types — mostly p4d and a few T4s for smaller models. We currently use an internal KV cache and ephemeral pods for session handling.
[03:01] Maya: Helpful, thanks. Pilot goal from Redwood's side is to show predictable latency and unit cost predictable across a small set of endpoints. We'll propose either Redwood Private in your VPC or Redwood Dedicated depending on whether you need the control plane in your account.

[04:12] Liam: Quick security note — anything that touches PHI has to meet our internal policy and HIPAA. We need audit logs, SSO, and KMS integration. Also, any egress to a hosted control plane is a red flag without contractual safeguards.
[04:31] Jordan: Understood. We have a Private offering that can run the control plane in your VPC — that addresses most data residency and egress concerns. We also support KMS integration and HSM via customer-managed keys. I'll share the security pack after the call.

[06:00] Anika: From a clinical perspective, we need explainability on model outputs and a way to flag when behavior drifts. We can't accept silent regressions.
[06:12] Ravi: We recommend setting up a quality monitoring hook — Redwood Optimize + evals that run on sample prompts. You can set regressions alerts tied to prompt sets; we can show a demo in the tech deep-dive.

[08:30] Ethan: A couple practical questions — how do we route traffic? We have multiple services that call inference; can we do route-based tokens or service-scoped API keys?
[08:44] Jordan: Yes, you can create route-level credentials and map them to projects in our Console. That gives per-route cost and latency breakdowns. We can also set quotas.

[10:15] Sofia: Timeline — we need something in 6 to 8 weeks for a pilot because compliance review and clinical validation windows are tight. Is that realistic?
[10:26] Maya: That's tight but doable. Typical pilot is 4 weeks of lab tests then a 2-4 week live sampling period. We'll need your infra folks to be available for VPC peering and security reviews.

[12:00] Ethan: Network requirements — we prefer VPC peering and no internet-facing control plane. Can you send a sample diagram?
[12:08] Ravi: Yep, I'll produce a network diagram showing VPC peering, private control plane endpoints, and NAT/egress flows. We'll include port lists and CIDR needs.

[14:45] Liam: What about logging retention and access controls? Our auditors want 12 months of immutable logs and RBAC with SSO.
[14:55] Jordan: We can configure log export to a customer-owned S3 bucket with immutable retention policies. SSO via SAML and RBAC is supported. I'll include specifics in the security packet.

[17:20] Sofia: Pilot KPIs — here's what matters: P95 latency under 350ms for our 1–2k token prompts, availability 99.9% during business hours, and cost per 1M tokens at or below our current spend once factoring in caching. Also clinical accuracy metrics (F1/recall) per prompt set.
[17:40] Ravi: For P95 at that length, we typically recommend batching configs and KV cache warm-ups. We'll share quantization guidance if you choose a compatible open model.

[20:10] Ethan: Customer-managed model hosting is a requirement — we want the model weights stored in our account, not Redwood's. Is that supported?
[20:18] Jordan: For Private deployments, yes — you can run the model artifact within your infra and our runtime will orchestrate. For Hosted we host artifacts. We'll clarify that in the doc.

[22:00] Anika: Who's the clinical contact on Redwood side for validation support? We might need help creating prompt suites and eval criteria.
[22:10] Maya: I can coordinate with our Applied ML folks to help build the eval harness and define acceptance tests. We'll schedule dedicated time during the pilot.

[25:40] Ethan: Any blockers from Redwood's side we should be aware of?
[25:45] Ravi: No blockers per se; the main items are network access and permissions for the pilot agent. We'll need a role in your account with limited IAM permissions for deployment and monitoring.

[28:00] Sofia: Pricing concerns — our execs will push back on committing to Dedicated without seeing a clear ROI vs our current self-hosted solution.
[28:10] Jordan: Understood. For the pilot we'll provide a usage-based estimate and a comparative cost analysis that factors in ops overhead — that usually helps surface the true TCO.

[30:50] Liam: Also need to confirm data deletion policies. If we stop the pilot, how quickly can data be purged?
[30:58] Jordan: We support configurable retention and can purge or redact logs on request. For Private, data never leaves your VPC unless you opt in.

[33:20] (Speaker 2 — occasional mislabel):
[33:25] Maya: Ok, let's map owners and timeline — Sofia and Liam to complete compliance questionnaire by 2026-12-21. Jordan to send security pack and pricing by 2026-12-22. Ravi to share network diagram by 2026-12-23. Schedule tech deep-dive on 2026-12-24.

[35:00] Anika: For clinical validation, we'll want to run a blind A/B on a subset of cases. Are you able to dual-run requests and provide side-by-side outputs?
[35:12] Ravi: Yes, we can route duplicated traffic to both endpoints and collect outputs for offline comparison. We'll include sampling guidance so we don't double-charge tokens during the pilot.

[38:45] Ethan: Can we run a small synthetic stress test first? Maybe 1k requests over 10 minutes to validate autoscaling behavior.
[38:55] Ravi: Absolutely — we'll craft a synthetic workload and a runbook for the stress test. We'll also capture token-level latency and throughput metrics.

[41:00] Sofia: Any legal/procurement touchpoints? We have a vendor security review and a legal standard contract review. 
[41:10] Jordan: We'll introduce you to our contracts rep after this call so they can start the security and legal right away. We'll also include a standard DPA and HIPAA addendum draft.

[44:20] Maya: Quick note on observability — the Console will give you per-route cost and latency, traces, and token breakdowns. You can set alerts for regression or cost spiking. We'll walk through that in the deep-dive.

[46:00] Jordan: Alright, final recap — owners and dates: Liam and Sofia complete compliance Q by 12/21; Jordan sends security pack + pricing 12/22; Ravi network diagram 12/23; tech deep-dive 12/24 10am EST. Pilot scope: 30 days, 3 endpoints, synthetic + live sampling.
[46:28] Sofia: Sounds good. Thank you.
[46:32] Anika: Thanks, appreciate it.
[46:35] Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts and calendar invites.

[46:50] (call ends)
